title: `!` on a durable input is refused: the smallest truthiness inspection is still an inspection
notes: The unary member of the family. It exists as its own case because `||`, `??` and `===` are all binary, and a walk that rejected unsupported BINARY operators would leave this one to fold to a constant boolean that type-checks. The declared position is the `!` token for the same reason as the `typeof` case: the unrepresentable expression is the unary one. specification/durable-execution.mdx:71 (Flow Purity): 'Runtime-dependent control flow MUST be represented explicitly in Plan IR. The compiler MUST reject an operation that would inspect a symbolic value without a corresponding IR representation.' specification/durable-execution.mdx:59 (Flow): 'The compiler MUST lower the function's checked syntax, control flow, and data flow into Plan IR. It MUST NOT invoke the source function with proxy or symbolic JavaScript values to discover the graph.' The declared position is the start of the expression or statement the lowering could not represent, which is where both backends anchor the durable-subset rules the corpus already pins (17-durable/statement-branch-fails-closed anchors SMITHERS4106 on its `if` token). Written from the two sentences above rather than from an implementation: the second one is the rule, and the first one names the technique — discovery by proxy — that turns a refusal into a silently folded Plan. This case pins CURRENT behaviour on the normative `.sm` path; it was not failing before the durable lane's fix, because that fix hardened the RUNTIME authoring guard (`poc/src/durable/authoring.ts`), a different entry point, and the `.sm` path already failed closed on this form. Its value is the other direction: the `.sm` rule was unpinned for this form, so a lowering that started folding it would have been observed by nothing. A `messageContains` is declared here and the reason is specific to this position. At the declared column three expressions start at once — the identifier `input`, the projection `input.mode`, and the operator expression built over it — so code and position ALONE are satisfied by a backend that refused the identifier and never looked at the operator, which is a different program passing the same expectation. The fragment is the SyntaxKind this program actually wrote, not the rule: it differs across the six SMITHERS4111 cases in this area (BinaryExpression / TypeOfExpression / PrefixUnaryExpression), which is what makes it legitimate under README §'A worked example of when NOT to declare one'. The JS reference prints `unsupported durable expression BinaryExpression` where the Go fork prints `unsupported durable expression KindBinaryExpression`, so the smallest fragment carrying the promise is the bare kind name, which is a substring of both — measured on both backends, not assumed. Verified enforced by mutating the fragment to a different SyntaxKind, watching both backends print the message diff, and restoring the file byte-identically (sha256 compared before and after).
